summary:
Red team of the extraction of Lawrence–Venkatesh, Diophantine problems and p-adic period mappings (Invent. Math. 221 (2020) 893–999; arXiv:1807.02721v3). Both recorded texts were re-downloaded and their hashes match; there is no later arXiv version and no Crossref correction. Three parallel readers read the whole paper by section groups, and I re-checked every finding in the text and in the published version. 12 findings: 2 high, 3 medium, 7 low.

Where the work is sound: every numbered result of §§2–12 has an item, E1–E3 are right, and the routes create no cycle. 'Only 67 items' comes from bundling, not from skipped numbered results. The gaps are in statuses, in imported inputs and in errata that were not applied.

High:
(1) The six §3 items (Gauss–Manin transport, monodromy group, Lemmas 3.1 and 3.3, crystalline transport, Proposition 3.4) are stated for any smooth proper family over a base of any dimension, in any degree. They are marked planned at MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.2–LV.4, but those layers plan only H¹ of abelian-by-finite families, and Proposition 3.4 only over curves. Route 1's brief tells the Part II to import period maps from LV.2–LV.3 for the hypersurface families of §§9–10, so nothing plans them. The period domain H/H* has no item at all.
(2) Bakker–Tsimerman's Ax–Schanuel theorem (Theorem 9.1) is 'planned' at LD.6. LD.6 treats Ax–Schanuel as an outside input, and the accepted supplier LogicAndDefinabilityPartII covers only Shimura varieties. So the transcendence input of Theorem 10.1 has no owner.

Medium:
(3) Six items copy statements corrected by confirmed roadmap errata; Lemma 2.8 and Lemma 2.12 are false or vacuous as written. The review's gap wrongly says the corrected statements are used.
(4) LV Lemma 2.6 and G-irreducibility get two owners: this extraction sends them to the Part II, PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25 route 2 sends the GSp case to LV.1. The brief also ignores erratum E28, which says the printed proof of Lemma 2.6 fails.
(5) The imported theorems have no items: Chebotarev, Weil/Deligne purity, D_cris full faithfulness, Faltings's comparison, Fontaine–Laffaille, the trace formula, Richardson and others.

Low:
(6) The Hermite–Minkowski and Grassmannian library claims are broader than the Mathlib declarations.
(7) The S-unit theorem and Mordell statements have other owners (DT.2; RP.4/R28.5).
(8) G-complete reducibility is also planned at LP2.
(9) The symplectic case of hypersurface monodromy is at LPV.5.
(10) Eight items have unfaithful statements or locators, including Theorem 10.1's monodromy hypothesis and Proposition 10.2's conclusion.
(11) Seven unrecorded source mistakes, including gaps in Lemma 2.10 and Lemma 10.5.
(12) Lemma 2.2 belongs at R01.1.

The review changed only verdicts, locators and gaps; apart from the gap text in (3) it introduced no error. Disclosures: this session wrote FIX-RT-AUDIT-07 (finding 7), red-teamed PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25 (findings 1 and 4) and wrote PAPER-DELIGNE-80 (cited in finding 5).

The string cc-f805bf occurs in none of the four target files (result.json, .md, review.json, the review report), and git log shows only the two commits f16139a6 and 0c27998a on them.

Disclosure. This session wrote FIX-RT-AUDIT-07, whose finding /6 recorded that DT.2 misses MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.6 (the S-unit theorem) and left a maintainer note because LV.6 is not an atlas stage; finding 7 touches this. It red-teamed PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25 (PR #4718): its confirmed finding /13 is the same kind of error as finding 1 here (a period map planned at LV.3 beyond LV.3's generality), and it did not flag Betts–Stix route 2, which finding 4 shows conflicts with this extraction's route 1. It also wrote PAPER-DELIGNE-80, whose route to DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.7 finding 5 cites as the owner of purity for smooth proper varieties (no correction to it is asked), and PAPER-SCHOLZE-13, and red-teamed PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19 (PR #4742); no finding touches the last two.

Sources. arXiv:1807.02721v3 re-downloaded on 30 September 2026, sha256 e3013516…c6b9b, matching the record; the arXiv API lists v3 (25 October 2019) as the last version and /abs/1807.02721v4 returns 404. The published article (Invent. Math. 221 (2020) 893–999) re-downloaded from the BIMSA copy, sha256 588e450a…db43bd, matching the review's record; printed page = PDF page + 892. Crossref for doi:10.1007/s00222-020-00966-7 lists no update-to, updated-by or relation. Every passage quoted in a finding was also located in the published text layer and persists there.

Reading. Three parallel readers read every line of arXiv v3 by section groups (pp. 1–25, 25–51, 51–76 with the bibliography), compared every item in range for statement, hypotheses and locator, listed every result used without an item and every slip; page images were rendered for pp. 53, 58, 62, 63, 64 and 69. I personally re-read and re-checked, in the text layer, every passage a finding quotes: §3.1–3.5 (pp. 15–20), Lemmas 2.2–2.12 (pp. 9–15), §4.1 (p. 21), Theorem 5.4 and its proof (pp. 26–27), Lemma 6.3 and Prop. 5.3, §7.2 (E3), Lemmas 8.2–8.3, §§9.1–9.2 (pp. 52–53), §10.1–10.2 (pp. 55–57), Lemmas 10.4–10.5 and their proofs (pp. 60–64), Proposition 10.6, and §12 (E2).

Coverage of numbered results. Every numbered Lemma, Proposition, Theorem, Corollary and Definition of §§2–12 (Lemmas 2.1–2.14, Def. 2.7, Lemmas 3.1–3.3, Prop. 3.4, Thm 4.1, Lemmas 4.2–4.4, Defs 5.1–5.2, Prop. 5.3, Thm 5.4, Lemmas 6.1–6.4 and the Sublemma, Prop. 7.1, Defs 7.2–7.3, Lemma 7.4, Thm 8.1, Lemmas 8.2–8.11, Prop. 8.5, Thm 9.1, Cor. 9.2, Lemma 9.3, Thm 10.1, Prop. 10.2, Lemmas 10.3–10.5, Prop. 10.6, Lemmas 11.1–11.2, Prop. 11.3, Lemma 11.4, Lemma 12.1) has an item; the omissions are imported external theorems and objects (findings 1, 5).

Statuses. Library: NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Basic.lean:496), Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean:442) and Module.Grassmannian (Mathlib/RingTheory/Grassmannian.lean:68) read at Mathlib 082e2d3; the Dirichlet citation holds, the other two are narrower than claimed (finding 6). Tau Ceti f790474 searched (declarations.tsv) for Chebotarev, Hermite, Eulerian numbers, flag varieties and Lagrangian Grassmannians: none of these is present beyond the preparatory Chebotarev lemmas.

Planned layers. Read in full: research/blueprint/roadmaps/MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.json (draft, review needs_changes, not in data/atlas.json; allowed as a planned target by PROTOCOL section 16) with all twelve LV stages, the statements of every LV.2–LV.4 node of its 132-node packet, keyword searches over all 132 nodes, and all 73 of its supplier requests; LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.6 and its 13-node packet; FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.1, R28.5 and their packet nodes; DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence DT.2; HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.4; ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1; PadicHodgeTheory R06.2, R06.5, R06.6, P7; CohomologyComparisons CP.0–CP.6; DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.0–DWP.10; WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.1–R34.6; WeilConjectures WC.0–WC.7; LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0–LPV.7; LanglandsParameterStacks LP2 and its packet. Each planned item was checked against what its layer plans in the paper's generality: 41 planned items, of which the six §3 items (finding 1) and Theorem 9.1 (finding 2) fail, and s-unit-theorem/theorem-5-4 have other statement owners (finding 7).

Missing items searched. Keyword search over all 1968 atlas stage descriptions for G-complete reducibility, Richardson, Katz–Messing, Mumford–Tate, Hodge torus, Griffiths/Jacobian ring, Eulerian, hypersurface monodromy (Beauville, Lefschetz), Fontaine–Laffaille, Tannakian, Mazur, Strassmann, Gauss–Manin; hits read (LP2, LPV.5, R07.3, C5/CR.7/A4); findings 8 and 9 record the two genuine overlaps. The rest of the 23 missing items have no owner.

Routes and order. Route 1 (part-ii) coalesces with PAPER-LAWRENCE-SAWIN-25 route 1 (same id, parent, area arithmeticgeometry, a valid galaxy id); DESIGN-MordellLawrenceVenkateshPartII and its review are pending in the queue, so no design exists to compare with. Route 2 (source, LV.1). No cycles: MordellLawrenceVenkatesh has no stage-edge or link-file or packet link from any of its stages to another roadmap, so nothing it supplies can be upstream of its own inputs, and the Part II's imports (LV.2–LV.3, LD.6, Chebotarev Layer 10) do not depend on it.

Other extractions compared. PAPER-LAWRENCE-SAWIN-25 (items /6, /43, /44, /45, /71, /76 and route 1 brief); PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25 (routes 2–5 into LV.1–LV.3 and LV.7, items /12, /13, /28) and its red team; PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 (route 1, LogicAndDefinabilityPartII, accepted); PAPER-BAKKER-KLINGLER-TSIMERMAN-20 (routes to LD.6 and DegeneratingHodgeStructures; neither plans Ax–Schanuel for variations of Hodge structure); PAPER-DELIGNE-80 (purity routed to DWP.5–DWP.8 and Lefschetz-pencil monodromy to LPV.5, consistent with findings 5 and 9), PAPER-SCHOLZE-13 (routes to P8, PerfectoidSpaces, A1, AdicSpacesPartII, AI.3) and PAPER-BALAKRISHNAN-DOGRA-MULLER-ETAL-19 (routes to NC.2, NC.5, ED.6, R13.5): none routes the period-map or crystalline-comparison material of this paper elsewhere.

Source issues. E1 re-verified: degree-d forms in n+1 variables span C(n+d, d) dimensions, the printed C(n+d, d−1) − 1 gives d(d+1)/2 − 1 for n = 1; (10.8) survives. E2 re-verified: g_N has frequencies up to 2N, the tail is 2Σ_{r≤2N} x^r ≤ 3x^{2N} for x ≥ 4, and (2N+1)²/‖g_N‖² = 3(2N+1)/(8N²+8N+3) ≤ 3/(4N). E3 re-verified: G_q is undefined, Aff(q) is meant. All three persist at published pp. 971, 996, 941. The 28 roadmap errata (MordellLawrenceVenkatesh/E1–E28) were read, to avoid duplicates and to check which items use corrected statements (finding 3).

Review. The review changed only verdicts, locators, sourceVersions, the published-version gap and the new 'roadmap-errata' gap. Its published locators (pp. 971, 995–996, 941) are right. Its gap text claims the planned items use the roadmap's corrected statements, which is not so (finding 3); it introduced no other error.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-LAWRENCE-VENKATESH-20.result.json: items PAPER-LAWRENCE-VENKATESH-20/good-model-gm (planned LV.2), /monodromy-group, /lemma-3-1, /lemma-3-3 (planned LV.3), /crystalline-transport, /prop-3-4 (planned LV.4); route 1 (part-ii MordellLawrenceVenkateshPartII) brief
findings.claim: The §3 items are stated, as in the paper, for an arbitrary smooth proper family X → Y over a smooth base Y of any dimension, in any cohomological degree q, with period maps into a space of flags H (item /prop-3-4: '{y ∈ Y(O) : … ρ_y semisimple} lies in a proper K_v-analytic subvariety'; /crystalline-transport: 'H^q_dR(X_y/K_v)'). They are marked planned at MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.2–LV.4, but those layers and all their packet nodes plan only the degree-one cohomology of polarized abelian-by-finite families (Lagrangian Grassmannian targets), and Proposition 3.4 only 'for polarized abelian schemes over a curve'. Nothing in the atlas plans Gauss–Manin transport, the complex and v-adic period maps, Lemmas 3.1/3.3 or Proposition 3.4 for H^q of a general smooth proper family over a higher-dimensional base, nor the period domain H of flags with given Hodge numbers and its self-dual compact dual H* (the target of Φ_p in §§9–10, for which no item exists at all). Route 1's brief nevertheless tells the design job to import 'period maps and Gauss–Manin transport from MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.2–LV.3' for Lemma 9.3 and Theorem 10.1, whose families are universal hypersurface families (primitive H^{n−1}, base of dimension C(n+d,d) − 1, orthogonal or symplectic flag varieties). So the higher-dimensional half has no supplier for its period maps, and six statuses are wrong in the paper's generality. The crystalline comparison for general smooth proper X is planned elsewhere (CohomologyComparisons CP.2 with PadicHodgeTheory R06.5), but the LV packet asks R06.5 only for 'the case i = 1 for abelian schemes'. This is the same kind of error as RT-PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25/13 (confirmed), which this session filed for Betts–Stix's item /28.
findings.evidence: Paper, arXiv v3 §3.1 p. 15 (published p. 913, unchanged): 'Let Y be a smooth K-variety, and π : X → Y a proper smooth morphism'; p. 16: 'Fixing a degree q ⩾ 0, we denote by ρ_y the representation of the Galois group G_K on the étale cohomology group'; Proposition 3.4, p. 19: 'X → Y is a smooth proper family over K, V is the degree q de Rham cohomology of a given fiber X_0 above y_0 ∈ Y(K), H a space of flags in V'; §9.2 p. 52: 'suppose additionally that X → Y is defined over Z[S^{-1}]. Fix p ∉ S and y_0 ∈ Y(Z_p). As before we can form the p-adic period map (9.2) Φ_p : residue disk around y_0 in Y(Q_p) → H*_{Q_p}'; §10.1 p. 55: 'V_0 = H^d(X_{0,C}, Q)_prim … Aut(V_0 ⊗ C, ⟨−,−⟩)'. research/blueprint/roadmaps/MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.json: LV.2 'for polarized abelian schemes over a finite étale cover of the base'; LV.3 'specialized to the degree-one cohomology of abelian-by-finite families'; LV.4 '*LV Proposition 3.4* for polarized abelian schemes over a curve'. research/blueprint/packets/MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.json: every LV.3/LV.4 period-map node opens with 'Setting P: … a good model over 𝒪 = 𝒪_S of an abelian-by-finite family X → Y' → Y of relative dimension d'; node LV.2/de-rham-bundle is 'ℋ := π_* H¹_dR(𝒳/𝒴')'; node LV.4/proposition-3-4 is titled '(LV Proposition 3.4, for curves)'; the request to PadicHodgeTheory:R06.5 ends '(the case i = 1 for abelian schemes suffices)'. PAPER-LAWRENCE-SAWIN-25 route 1 brief: 'there the method is run on the primitive cohomology of an abelian-by-finite family over a curve'.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-LAWRENCE-VENKATESH-20.result.json: item PAPER-LAWRENCE-VENKATESH-20/bakker-tsimerman (planned LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.6); route 1 brief ('importing Bakker–Tsimerman from LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.6')
findings.claim: Theorem 9.1 (Bakker–Tsimerman's Ax–Schanuel theorem for variations of Hodge structure) is marked planned at LD.6, and route 1 tells the design job to import it from there. LD.6 does not plan it: it plans o-minimal structures, Pila–Wilkie and Pila–Zannier applications, and lists Ax–Schanuel theorems as independent inputs that an application 'must provide'. The item's own note concedes this ('LD.6 … takes Ax–Schanuel theorems as independently acquired functional-transcendence inputs'). The LD packet has 13 nodes, none about Ax–Schanuel or period maps. The accepted extraction PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 created the supplier LD.6 lacks, the Part II LogicAndDefinabilityPartII ('Part II: functional transcendence and Ax–Schanuel for Shimura varieties'), whose brief says LD.6 'names … Ax-Lindemann/Ax-Schanuel inputs among the primary proofs it must acquire; this Part II supplies those inputs', but it covers only Shimura varieties, not period maps of arbitrary variations of Hodge structure. So Theorem 9.1, on which Corollary 9.2, Lemma 9.3, Theorem 10.1 and Proposition 10.2 all rest, has no owner, and the Part II design would import a theorem nobody builds. PAPER-LAWRENCE-SAWIN-25/76 makes the same claim (outside this target).

Suppose that V ⊂ Y × H* is algebraic … Then the projection of U to Y is contained in a proper (“weak Mumford-Tate”) subvariety'; p. 2: 'To prove this higher-dimensional result, we use a very recent theorem of Bakker and Tsimerman, the Ax–Schanuel theorem for period mappings'.
findings.fix: Mark /bakker-tsimerman missing and route it (part-ii) to LogicAndDefinabilityPartII, coalescing with PAPER-MOK-PILA-TSIMERMAN-19 route 1: its brief should add the Ax–Schanuel theorem for period maps of polarized integral variations of Hodge structure (Bakker–Tsimerman, Invent. Math. 217 (2019), Theorem 1.1, as quoted in LV Theorem 9.1), with weak Mumford–Tate subvarieties, as a second final theorem generalizing the Shimura case. In route 1's brief replace 'importing Bakker–Tsimerman from LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.6' by 'importing Bakker–Tsimerman's Ax–Schanuel theorem for variations of Hodge structure from LogicAndDefinabilityPartII'. findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-LAWRENCE-VENKATESH-20.result.json: items PAPER-LAWRENCE-VENKATESH-20/lemma-2-3, /lemma-2-8, /lemma-2-12, /prop-5-3, /lemma-6-3, /lemmas-8-2-8-3; gap 'roadmap-errata'; the review's notes
findings.claim: PROTOCOL section 18 requires 'Items and nodes use the corrected statements'. Six items copy statements that confirmed errata in research/blueprint/errata/MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.json correct, and two of them are false as written. (a) /lemma-2-8 keeps 'η²|_{K_v^×} = χ·Norm^w_{K_v/Q_p}' on all of K_v^× (erratum E3, 'a stated result'): for K = Q, v = p and η = χ_cyc (pure of weight 2, locally algebraic) the ratio η²/Norm² sends p to p^{−2} (with either normalisation of Art_{Q_p}), which is not of finite order; the identity holds only on O_{K_v}^×. (b) /lemma-2-12 keeps 'for all i, j some g ∈ G has π_i(g), π_j(g) unipotent with fixed spaces of different dimensions' (E22): for i = j the condition is unsatisfiable, so the item as stated is vacuous; i ≠ j is needed. (c) /lemmas-8-2-8-3 keeps 'the preimages of a simple closed curve e are linearly independent' (E13) and the unqualified 'rank of Mon(D_e^M) − Id determines the cycle type' (E14): for e bounding a disk in Y − {y} every preimage bounds a disk upstairs, so all classes vanish. (d) /lemma-2-3 keeps 'unramified outside S' with S containing no place above p (E2), which excludes every geometric representation it is applied to. (e) /prop-5-3 omits the odd residue characteristic and the §3 good-reduction conditions on v (E7). (f) /lemma-6-3 omits 0 ≠ W ≠ V, non-emptiness of A (E10) and the similitude condition on φ (E25). The review's gap says 'The items planned in MordellLawrenceVenkatesh use that roadmap's corrected statements', but the items in this file do not, and the gap's item list omits /lemma-2-3, /lemma-2-8 and /lemmas-8-2-8-3. The review also states that 'All compared statements match their items', which is true only because both copy the printed text.
findings.evidence: research/blueprint/errata/MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.json (review verdicts 'confirmed'): E2 'Use a finite set T = S ∪ {w : w divides p} in the finiteness lemma'; E3 'The identity holds on the local units: η²|_{O_{K_v}^*} = χ · Norm_{K_v/Q_p}^w … It does not hold on all of K_v^*'; E7 'explicitly restrict to odd residue characteristic and to the §3 good-reduction setup'; E10 'Require 0≠W≠V … and specify that its open subset A is nonempty'; E13 'Require e to be nonseparating in Y'; E14 'Take a nonseparating simple closed curve … and a positive sufficiently divisible M'; E22 'Add i≠j to the second hypothesis'; E25 'require φ to be a semilinear similitude'. Paper, arXiv v3 p. 12 (published p. 908, unchanged): 'η²|_{K_v^*} = χ · Norm^w_{K_v/Q_p}, where χ has finite order'; p. 14: 'For 1 ⩽ i, j ⩽ N, there exists g ∈ G such that π_i(g) and π_j(g) are unipotent with fixed spaces of different dimensions'; p. 42: 'Lemma 8.2. Let e be a simple closed curve in Y − {y}. Then the classes of the preimages [e_1], …, [e_k] in the homology of Z are linearly independent'. The items quote these verbatim.
findings.fix: Restate the six items in corrected form: /lemma-2-3 with T = S ∪ {places above p}; /lemma-2-8 on O_{K_v}^× (keeping 'w is even and the Hodge–Tate weight at v is w/2'); /lemma-2-12 with i ≠ j; /prop-5-3 with v of odd residue characteristic and the §3.1 conditions (K_v/Q_p unramified, no place of S above p); /lemma-6-3 with 0 ≠ W ≠ V, A nonempty and φ a semilinear similitude; /lemmas-8-2-8-3 for nonseparating e and sufficiently divisible M. findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-LAWRENCE-VENKATESH-20.result.json: items PAPER-LAWRENCE-VENKATESH-20/lemma-2-6 and /g-semisimplification in route 1 (part-ii MordellLawrenceVenkateshPartII); research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25.result.json route 2 (source, MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.1) with its items /12, /13
findings.claim: Two accepted extractions give LV Lemma 2.6 and the notion of G-irreducibility two owners. PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25 route 2 (accepted) sends 'The symplectic form of Faltings's lemma ([LV20, Lemma 2.6]) and GSp-irreducibility' to LV.1. This extraction sends Lemma 2.6 for every reductive G, and G-irreducibility, G-complete reducibility and G-semisimplification, to the Part II MordellLawrenceVenkateshPartII. The GSp case is a special case of both items, and LV.1 is upstream of the Part II, so the same lemma would be planned twice at two levels of generality (PROTOCOL section 15: plan a notion once, in its most general form, in the most foundational roadmap that needs it). In addition, route 1's brief presents 'Faltings finiteness for reductive targets (Lemma 2.6)' as a result to import from the paper, but confirmed erratum MordellLawrenceVenkatesh/E28 says the printed proof fails ('Parametrize conjugated representations using the right centralizer Z_{GL_n}(L)(Q_p), not L(Q_p). A complete finiteness proof then needs an appropriate finiteness result for embeddings/orbits …'), and E27 corrects the domain of the refined statement. Neither the item nor the brief mentions this, so the design job would plan a proof that does not work. Disclosure: this session red-teamed PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25 (PR #4718) and did not flag its route 2.
findings.evidence: PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25.result.json route 2: 'The symplectic form of Faltings's lemma ([LV20, Lemma 2.6]) and GSp-irreducibility belong beside the semisimple Faltings lemma that LV.1 already plans', items /12 ('it is GSp-irreducible if … the image does not lie in a proper parabolic subgroup of GSp') and /13 ('Lemma 2.4: symplectic Faltings lemma (cited) … [LV20, Lemma 2.6]'); its review: route 2 'accept'. This extraction's route 1 items include /g-semisimplification and /lemma-2-6; its brief: 'G-irreducibility, G-complete reducibility and G-semisimplification with Lemmas 2.4–2.5 and Faltings finiteness for reductive targets (Lemma 2.6), shared with Lawrence–Sawin's disconnected-group version'. findings.claim: Every numbered result of the paper has an item, but the external theorems the proofs import are almost all absent, contrary to PROTOCOL section 16 ('Every definition, construction and key theorem the paper uses or proves on the way to its main results is an item'). Missing, with the owner that plans each: (1) the Chebotarev density theorem, used to choose v in §4.1, in Theorem 5.4 and to choose ℓ in Lemma 10.4 (Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10; the Tau Ceti library at f790474 has only preparatory lemmas under TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/, no density theorem); (2) purity and integrality of Frobenius on the cohomology of the fibres, without which Lemmas 2.3 and 2.6 cannot be applied to ρ_y: Weil's theorem for abelian varieties in the curve case (DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.1) and Deligne's purity for the smooth projective hypersurfaces of Theorem 10.1 and Lemma 12.1 (Weil I at DWP.4 and WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.5; the smooth proper form at DWP.7, where PAPER-DELIGNE-80, written by this session, routes it); (3) unramifiedness of ρ_y outside S and places above p (smooth proper base change; Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5); (4) full faithfulness of D_cris on crystalline representations, filtered φ-modules and weak admissibility, used in §3.5 ([8, Prop. 9.1.9]), §6 and the proof of Lemma 4.4 (PadicHodgeTheory R06.2); item /crystalline-transport merges this with Faltings's comparison theorem [16] (CohomologyComparisons CP.2); (5) the Berthelot–Ogus comparison and crystalline Frobenius of (3.9) (CrystallineCohomology CR.2, CR.3), and the existence of the Gauss–Manin connection and its de Rham–Betti compatibility ([23] Katz–Oda; ComplexComparisonPartII C5); (6) Fontaine–Laffaille theory and the comparison of Tannakian fibre functors in footnote 10, the core of the Hodge-torus argument of Lemma 10.4 (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.3; [12, §3]); (7) Strassmann's theorem, which turns Lemma 3.3 into finiteness on a curve (planned as node LV.3/strassmann); (8) Riemann existence, GAGA and the profinite fundamental group of a punctured curve used in §§5 and 7.3 (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.3, ComplexComparisonPartII C2), and the Weil pairing on H¹_et(Y_K̄, Z/(q−1)) in Theorem 5.4 (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.2); (9) the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula for a smooth hypersurface in Lemma 12.1; (10) Richardson's theorem [34, Thm 7.1] and finiteness of H¹(Q_p, S) [41] in Lemma 2.6, and the local analytic Nullstellensatz [10, §3.4], Noetherianity of the Tate algebra and Krull's intersection theorem in Lemma 9.3, which nothing in the atlas plans. The prerequisites list omits Faltings 1989 [16], Katz–Oda 1968 [23] and Richardson 1967 [34]. So the extraction cannot be used to check the Part II's imports, and three of these (1, 2, 6) are load-bearing for Theorem 10.1.

findings.claim: Both library claims are broader than the declarations. (a) /hermite-minkowski states finiteness of extensions of K 'of bounded degree unramified outside a finite set of primes (equivalently of bounded discriminant)', which is the form used in Lemma 2.3, §4.1 and §6. Mathlib's theorem is Hermite's theorem over Q for bounded absolute discriminant only; passing from 'degree n, unramified outside S' to a discriminant bound needs the bound on the different at ramified primes and a relative version over K, and the item's 'equivalently' hides that step: bounded degree and ramification in S bound the discriminant only through the bound on the different at the primes of S (for example v_p(disc) ≤ n − 1 + n·v_p(n) for a degree-n extension), and the paper needs it relative to K. The form used is exactly the node FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.1/hermite-minkowski-finiteness-of-extensions-unramified-outside-S, which the LV packet imports. (b) /grassmannian claims Module.Grassmannian as 'the ambient variety of the flag and Lagrangian period domains' and cites §3.4, but §3.4's H is a partial flag variety and §6's H_v is a Weil restriction of a Lagrangian Grassmannian; Mathlib has neither (the LV packet plans LGr at LV.3/lagrangian-grassmannian). The locator '§6 (Gr(V_v, g))' also copies erratum MordellLawrenceVenkatesh/E26 (should be Gr(V_v, d)).

findings.claim: The extraction and its review say nothing in the atlas owns Serre's G-complete reducibility. LanglandsParameterStacks LP2:semisimple-characters plans exactly Serre's definition (image in a parabolic implies image in a Levi) for L-parameters, with the closed-orbit characterisation. It is over an algebraically closed coefficient field and for Weil-group parameters, so it does not cover LV's K-rational version (K = Q_p, K-parabolics) or ρ^ss, but the general notion should be planned once (PROTOCOL section 15), and the Part II design should know that a second definition exists.
findings.evidence: research/blueprint/packets/LanglandsParameterStacks.json node LP2:semisimple-characters/semisimple-parameters-and-closed-orbits: 'an L-parameter phi … is SEMISIMPLE if whenever the image of phi is contained in a parabolic subgroup of G-hat semidirect W_E, it is contained in a Levi subgroup of that parabolic … semisimplicity is equivalent to the G-hat-orbit of phi in Z^1(W_E,G-hat)_L being CLOSED.' Paper, arXiv v3 p. 10: 'the representation ρ is G-c.r., or completely reducible relative to G, if for any parabolic subgroup P ⩽ G defined over K containing the image ρ(Γ), there exists a Levi factor L ⩽ P, defined over K, which also contains this image.'
findings.fix: Note in /g-semisimplification and in route 1's brief (or at its new owner, see finding 4) that LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:semisimple-characters plans the same notion for L-parameters over algebraically closed fields; the general K-rational definition, ρ^ss and Serre's Propositions 3.3 and 4.2 should be planned once and LP2's node should cite it.

findings.claim: The item says nothing plans the large monodromy of universal hypersurface families. LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.5 plans Deligne's theorem that the monodromy of a Lefschetz pencil with odd-dimensional fibres is open (hence Zariski dense) in Sp of the vanishing part, which gives the symplectic case of the density LV need (hypersurfaces of odd dimension n − 1) after restricting the universal family to a pencil and comparing ℓ-adic with Betti monodromy. Only the orthogonal case (even n − 1) and the finite-index statement of Beauville are genuinely missing. Route 1's brief should import LPV.5 rather than plan the symplectic case again.
findings.evidence: research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles.json LPV.5 'Irreducibility and open symplectic monodromy': 'For odd n, prove that the compact monodromy image is **open** in Sp(V), not just Zariski dense … Sources: Deligne I 5.3–5.11'. Paper, arXiv v3 p. 56: 'Note that this family indeed has large monodromy image by [4]' ([4] Beauville, LNM 1194); (10.1) p. 55: 'has Zariski closure containing the identity component of the right-hand group'.
findings.fix: In /hypersurface-monodromy's note and route 1's brief: import the odd-dimensional (symplectic) case from LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.5 plus the Betti–ℓ-adic comparison, and plan in the Part II only the even-dimensional (orthogonal) case, following Beauville or Deligne's Weil II 4.4.

findings.claim: Item statements and locators that are not the source's (none is covered by an erratum). (a) /theorem-10-1: 'monodromy Zariski dense in the identity component of Aut(V₀, ⟨,⟩)' forces the image into the identity component; the source asks that the closure contain it; V₀ = H^d(X_{0,C}, Q)_prim with its intersection form is never defined in the item; and the finiteness addendum is stated as a result although the paper proves only non-density and calls its hypothesis 'an unrealistically strong assumption' (footnote 8). (b) /hypersurface-application: Proposition 10.2 concludes only that (10.4) and (10.5) hold; the item adds the Diophantine conclusion (which needs Theorem 10.1 and Beauville's theorem) and states it for 'smooth hypersurfaces with good reduction outside S … of the moduli space', whereas §1 bounds F_{n,d}(Z[S^{-1}]), integral points of the parameter space of forms, and p. 20 stresses that bounding Y(O) is not bounding good reduction. (c) /theorem-5-4 replaces condition (ii) ('K′ is linearly disjoint from Q(ζ_{q−1})') by the sufficient condition from the proof and never says q is prime. (d) /lemma-4-2 keeps only condition (i) on v and drops '(ii) the prime p of Q below v is unramified in K, (iii) no prime of S lies above p', which §3 needs. (e) /good-model-gm says the formal horizontal sections 'have coefficients in O_(v)': the source puts the connection coefficients a_{ij,k} in O_(v) and the solutions in K[[z]] (the radius |p|^{1/(p−1)} reflects factorial denominators); it also omits p > 2, K_v/Q_p unramified and no place of S above p. (f) /crystalline-transport attributes 'Faltings's comparison' to '[8, 9.1.9]', which is Brinon–Conrad's full-faithfulness statement; Faltings is [16]. (g) /lemma-10-5 is located at '§10.5 … pp. 62–63', but the statement is on p. 60 in §10.3 (only the proof is §10.5); /prop-5-3's proof runs to p. 34, not p. 33.

findings.claim: Unrecorded mistakes in the paper, none in the extraction or in research/blueprint/errata/MordellLawrenceVenkatesh.json; all persist in the published text. (i) Gap, Lemma 2.10 (p. 14, published p. 910): the proof applies Lemma 2.9, which assumes V 'crystalline at all primes above p', to Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} ρ; its restriction to G_{K_v} is ⊕_{u|v} Ind_{G_{L_u}}^{G_{K_v}} ρ, which is not crystalline when some L_u/K_v is ramified (for ρ trivial it is a permutation representation on which inertia acts nontrivially). The displayed computation switches to B_dR silently. Correction: state Lemma 2.9 for de Rham V (its proof, via Lemma 2.8 on det V, needs only local algebraicity); the paper's applications (§4.4, §6) have L unramified at v and are unaffected. Affects the proof. (ii) Gap in Lemma 10.5 (p. 60, published p. 975): the hypothesis bounds the centralizer of Frob^{crys}_{y₀}, but the proof (p. 64) applies Proposition 10.6 with 'z = dim Z(φ^ss)'. Since everything commuting with φ commutes with its semisimple part, Z(φ) ⊆ Z(φ^ss), so the hypothesis does not bound z (for φ unipotent, Z(φ^ss) is all of GAut). Correction: assume the bound for (Frob^{crys}_{y₀})^ss, which is what Lemma 10.4 supplies; Theorem 10.1 is unaffected. Affects a stated result. (iii) Misprint, proof of Theorem 5.4 (p. 26, published p. 928): 'q is not congruent to 1 mod ℓ for any prime ℓ that … is less than 8[K : Q]' includes ℓ = 2, and every odd prime q is ≡ 1 mod 2; 'odd prime ℓ' is meant (condition (i) says 'odd primes'). (iv) Misprint, proof of Lemma 10.4 (p. 62, published p. 978): Frobenius 'scale[s] the bilinear forms by ℓ' and pairs V_λ with V_{ℓλ^{-1}}; the pairing lands in H^{2d} ≅ Q_p(−d), so the factor is ℓ^d, V_{ℓ^dλ^{-1}} and λ² = ℓ^d. Affects nothing. (v) Misprint, Lemma 2.5 (p. 10, published p. 906): 'χ : G_m → P be a character' should be cocharacter (the item /lemmas-2-4-2-5 silently corrects it). (vi) Gap, Lemma 9.3 (p. 52): 'Fix p ∉ S' allows p = 2, but the period map on the whole residue disk rests on §3.3, which needs p > 2 (for p = 2 the radius |2|^{1/(2−1)} = |2| excludes the points with |z| = |2|); enlarge S to contain 2. Affects nothing. (vii) Misprint, p. 57 (published p. 971): 'the symmetric or adjoint square' should be 'symmetric or alternating square', as (10.2) has Sym² or ∧².

findings.claim: Lemma 2.2 (induction from a finite-index subgroup preserves semisimplicity in characteristic 0; a representation is semisimple iff its restriction to a finite-index normal subgroup is) is general representation theory of abstract groups, not specific to the Lawrence–Venkatesh method.
